Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

status noun

standing in society

also social status, standing, social standing, rank, position in society

classical

Cic. Fam. 4.14.1: mē meam prīstinam dignitātem obtinēre

dignitās, dignitātis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

standing, rank, prestige

The standing a man has from office and conduct, and the respect it commands (Lewis & Short); the thing a Roman politician would least give up. It also means worthiness, and of persons and things, dignity, grandeur.

Other words

  • status, statūs m. — position, rank, condition in life

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.4.1: ex prīstinō statū nostrō; Cic. Leg. 1.23 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 25, 385 · Declension on Wiktionary

    One’s condition and place in society (Lewis & Short): free or slave, citizen or not, high or low; Traupman’s dē statū mulierum, on the status of women. First of all a way of standing, a posture; for the state things are in, see state (condition).

  • locus, locī m. — rank, birth: one’s place

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 5.25.1: summō locō nātus · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of birth and rank: summō locō nātus, of the highest birth; humilī locō, of low birth (Caes. BG 7.39).

Examples

  • ego autem, sī dignitās est bene dē rē pūblicā sentīre et bonīs virīs probāre quod sentiās, obtineō dignitātem meam

    but if standing means thinking rightly about the state and having good men approve what you think, I keep my standingCic. Fam. 4.14.1

  • nōn ut aliquid ex prīstinō statū nostrō retineāmus, sed ut quam honestissimē lūgeāmus

    not to keep anything of our former position, but to mourn as honourably as we canCic. Fam. 4.4.1

See also social, influence, state, position.
